_meta.purpose: Seed and reference data for the 'Kitchen' operations admin panel demo (Ahmedabad corporate boxed-lunch kitchen)
_meta.fictionalEntities: All companies, people, buildings, domains and phone numbers are fictional. Areas, roads and pincodes are real.

address.line1: Shed No. 14, Shreeji Food Park (fictional estate)
address.line2: Sarkhej–Bavla Highway, near Sarkhej Cross Roads

kitchen.locationRationale: Sarkhej is on the south-west edge of the city, where SG Highway meets the Sarkhej–Bavla highway. It has industrial and food-processing sheds and is about 5–15 km from the main client clusters (Prahlad Nagar, Bodakdev, Thaltej, Science City Road). GIFT City is about 35 km away via SG Highway. Alternatives are Changodar GIDC (382213, cheaper but farther out) and Odhav GIDC (382415, east side, far from the west-side office belt).
kitchen.workingDaysRationale: Many Ahmedabad companies (manufacturing, textiles, diamonds, traders, some pharma) work Saturdays, while IT and fintech work Mon–Fri. A six-day kitchen covers both, and Sunday is the usual weekly off for Indian commercial kitchens.

orderCutoff.rationale: Indian corporate tiffin and boxed-meal services usually lock next-day orders the previous evening (about 8–10 pm), so the kitchen can buy vegetables from the APMC or vendor early in the morning and start prep around 6 am for 12:30 delivery. Some services also offer a same-day 10:00 cutoff for small top-ups. Using 'previous working day' means Monday orders close on Saturday night.

stations.name: Roti / Tandoor
stations.description: Phulka, chapati, bajra rotla, thepla, paratha and tandoori roti/naan. Tawa and tandoor line with a dough-kneading machine.

stations.name: Curry & Gravy (Shaak)
stations.description: Gujarati dry and gravy shaak (sev tameta, ringan, undhiyu in season) plus North Indian gravies (paneer butter masala, chole, rajma). Bulk tilting pans and kadhai.

stations.name: Dal, Kadhi & Rice
stations.description: Gujarati khatti-meethi dal, dal fry, kadhi, jeera and steamed rice, khichdi and pulao. Steam-jacketed kettles and rice steamers.

stations.name: Farsan / Fry
stations.description: Dhokla, khaman, handvo and patra (steamed) plus fried items (samosa, kachori, bhajiya) and papad. Steamers and fryers.

stations.name: Sweets / Mithai
stations.description: Shrikhand, mohanthal, sukhdi, gulab jamun, kheer and basundi. Halwai section with milk-reduction kettles. Cold desserts move to the cold station for holding.

stations.name: Cold / Salad & Chaas
stations.description: Kachumber, sprout salad, raita, chutneys, chaas (buttermilk) and cold beverages. Chilled prep area at 5°C or below.

stations.name: Jain & Satvik Prep
stations.description: Separate counter and utensils for Jain and Swaminarayan orders (no onion, garlic or root vegetables) to prevent cross-contact. Common in Ahmedabad kitchens.

stations.name: Packing & Dispatch
stations.description: Portioning into compartment boxes, sealing, labelling (employee name, company, allergen and diet tags), and batching by company and delivery route.

allergens.name: Milk / Dairy
allergens.description: Ghee, paneer, dahi, chaas, khoya, cream and butter. Present in most Gujarati and North Indian dishes and sweets.

allergens.name: Cereals containing gluten (wheat, barley, rye, oats)
allergens.description: Wheat roti, thepla, puri, naan, sev and many farsan items. Hing (asafoetida) is often cut with wheat flour, so it is a hidden source.

allergens.name: Peanuts (groundnut)
allergens.description: Used heavily in Gujarati cooking: groundnut oil, crushed peanuts in shaak, poha, sabudana, chikki. Groundnut is the default frying oil in many Gujarati kitchens.

allergens.name: Tree nuts (cashew, almond, pistachio, walnut)
allergens.description: Cashew paste in Mughlai and North Indian gravies, plus almond and pistachio garnish on sweets (shrikhand, basundi, kheer).

allergens.name: Sesame (til)
allergens.description: Til in handvo, dhokla tempering, til chikki (especially around Uttarayan) and til oil. A major allergen in the EU, US and Codex, though not in FSSAI's mandatory list.

allergens.name: Mustard (rai)
allergens.description: Rai seeds in almost every Gujarati tadka, plus mustard oil and pickles (athanu). An EU allergen, not on FSSAI's mandatory list.

allergens.name: Soy
allergens.description: Tofu, soya chunks and soy sauce in Indo-Chinese dishes. On FSSAI's mandatory list.

allergens.name: Sulphites (≥10 mg/kg)
allergens.description: Found in some dried fruits, pickles, packaged vinegar and preserved items. On FSSAI's mandatory list.

allergens.name: Egg
allergens.description: Rare in a pure-veg kitchen, but some bought-in bakery items (cakes, mayonnaise, bread) contain egg. The kitchen should buy eggless bakery items. Kept here for completeness.

allergenNotes.fssai: Under the FSS (Labelling and Display) Regulations 2020, pre-packed food must declare allergens. The listed categories are cereals containing gluten, crustaceans, milk, eggs, fish, peanuts, tree nuts, soybeans and sulphite (≥10 mg/kg). Mustard and sesame are not mandatory in India, but list them because they are common in Gujarati food and expected by global clients (EU/US/Codex lists). Since 2022, FSSAI has also required food service businesses with a central licence or 10+ outlets to display allergen and veg/non-veg info on menus. A single-kitchen B2B caterer may not strictly be covered, but labelling every box is best practice.
allergenNotes.vegNonVegLogo: FSSAI requires the green dot-in-square vegetarian symbol on packaged food labels. Print it on every box label.
allergenNotes.uncertainty: The exact mandatory allergen list was recalled from the 2020 regulations. Search results confirmed that allergen declaration is mandatory but did not list every item. Check against Schedule/Regulation 5 of the FSSAI gazette before relying on it legally.

dietaryTags.name: Vegetarian
dietaryTags.definition: Lacto-vegetarian: no meat, fish or egg, dairy allowed. The default for every item in a pure-veg kitchen.

dietaryTags.name: Jain
dietaryTags.definition: No onion, garlic or root/underground vegetables (potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger, sweet potato), and usually no mushrooms or honey. Cooked fresh and served before sunset. Ginger is often replaced with dry ginger (sunth).

dietaryTags.name: Swaminarayan
dietaryTags.definition: No onion or garlic (root vegetables like potato are allowed), and hing is usually avoided too. Followers are a large community in Ahmedabad.

dietaryTags.name: Vegan
dietaryTags.definition: No animal products at all, so no ghee, paneer, dahi, chaas, butter, cream or honey. Cook in oil and use tofu instead of paneer.

dietaryTags.name: Gluten-free
dietaryTags.definition: No wheat, barley, rye or oats, and no hing cut with wheat (use gluten-free hing). Bajra, jowar, rice and nachni are fine. The kitchen cannot guarantee zero cross-contact with wheat.

dietaryTags.name: Eggless
dietaryTags.definition: Mainly matters for bakery and dessert items (cakes, brownies, mayo). Default in a pure-veg kitchen.

dietaryTags.name: Low-oil / Diabetic-friendly
dietaryTags.definition: Steamed or tawa-cooked with ≤1 tsp oil per portion, no added sugar or jaggery, and a millet or brown-rice base with high fibre and protein.

dietaryTags.name: High-protein
dietaryTags.definition: At least 20 g protein per portion (paneer, tofu, chana, rajma, sprouts).

dietaryTags.name: No onion / no garlic
dietaryTags.definition: A broader satvik tag that covers Swaminarayan diets and people fasting during Navratri, Shravan or Paryushan.

dietRecommendation: Run a 100% pure-vegetarian (and eggless) kitchen. In Ahmedabad this is effectively expected: many corporate canteens and caterers are pure-veg, the clientele is heavily Jain, Swaminarayan and Vaishnav, and a non-veg kitchen would lose Jain/Swaminarayan orders over cross-contact concerns. Offer Jain and no-onion/garlic versions of most dishes through a separate Jain station. Seed VEG and EGGLESS on every item.

portionSizes.name: Regular
portionSizes.description: Standard single-person box: about 450–550 g of food (2 phulka or 1 rotla, 1 shaak, 1 dal or kadhi, 1 rice portion, plus side).

portionSizes.name: Large
portionSizes.description: Hungry or plant-floor portion: about 650–750 g (4 phulka, larger shaak and rice). Common for factory and auto-component clients.

portionSizes.name: Mini / Half
portionSizes.description: Light lunch or snack-sized portion, about 300 g. Optional; some services sell 'half thali' at about 65% of the price.

packagingTypes.name: Bagasse 4/5-compartment box with lid
packagingTypes.notes: Compostable sugarcane-fibre box. Gujarat enforces the single-use plastic ban (2022), so this has become the default for disposable corporate lunch boxes. Costs about ₹8–₹14 per box. Holds hot dal poorly, so pair it with a sealed dal cup.

packagingTypes.name: Reusable stainless-steel tiffin (3/4 tier) in insulated bag
packagingTypes.notes: The classic Indian dabba. Collected the same afternoon or next day, washed and sanitised centrally. Needs deposit tracking per company and is popular with ESG-minded clients. Lowest per-meal cost after the initial investment.

packagingTypes.name: Sealed food-grade PP compartment tray (microwavable)
packagingTypes.notes: Tray film-sealed by machine. Tamper-evident and best for gravies and long transit (for example GIFT City). Uses heavier plastic, so check it complies with the plastic-ban thickness rules. About ₹10–₹18 per tray.

packagingTypes.name: Kraft paper bowl with PP-lined lid
packagingTypes.notes: For North Indian bowls, khichdi and salads. About ₹6–₹10.

packagingTypes.name: Aluminium foil tray / bulk chafing (for meetings)
packagingTypes.notes: For desserts or farsan sold by the tray (serves 10–12) and for meeting or event orders.

menuNotes.pricingBasis: Ahmedabad office-lunch tiffins usually cost ₹100–₹150 per meal, and an executive thali from a local Ahmedabad tiffin service is listed at ₹140 per plate (IndiaMART). Premium or paneer boxes reach ₹180–₹250. Selling prices here run from ₹110 to ₹240 for mains. 'costPriceINR' includes ingredients plus direct labour (about 45–55% of the selling price), but not packaging (₹8–₹18) or delivery.
menuNotes.portions: Dishes with usesPortions=true support Regular and Large. Large adds about ₹30–₹50 on the base box (suggest +₹40 on thali boxes and +₹35 on bowls), plus each option group's largeSurchargeINR for the portion-scaled groups (ROTI, RICE, DAL, PROTEIN). SIDE is never portioned.
menuNotes.optionPricing: Every option has a non-zero priceAddOnINR, as required. For required groups, the box's sellingPriceINR assumes the add-on of the chosen option is charged on top, so the cheapest real total for GUJ-001 is ₹130 + ₹5 phulka + ₹5 dal = ₹140.

priceTiers.name: Standard
priceTiers.notes: For SMEs and new clients. Usually monthly invoicing with 15-day credit.

priceTiers.name: Enterprise
priceTiers.notes: For clients with about 50+ boxes a day or an annual contract. Indian corporate caterers commonly give 5–10% volume discounts.

priceTiers.name: Partner
priceTiers.notes: For strategic or anchor clients and co-working partners (for example a GIFT City anchor tenant). This keeps a 37.5% gross margin on cost.

currency.format: Indian digit grouping: ₹1,23,456.00 (lakh/crore). Use Intl.NumberFormat('en-IN', {style:'currency', currency:'INR'}). Store amounts as integer paise or as decimals with 2 places.

notes.gst: Taxes are out of scope for the app: all totals are pre-tax. For context, restaurant and outdoor catering services in India usually charge 5% GST without input tax credit (18% in some cases), and invoices to companies need the client's GSTIN. Neither is modelled.
notes.uttarayan: In Ahmedabad, Jan 14 (Uttarayan) and Jan 15 (Vasi Uttarayan) are effectively both off. Offices empty out for kite flying, so close the kitchen both days even though only one is gazetted.
notes.diwali: Many Ahmedabad businesses stay closed or run thin from Diwali to Labh Pancham (5th day of the new year, about Nov 14 in 2026 and about Nov 3 in 2027). Expect very low order volume that week even on open days.
notes.navratri: Navratri (9 nights, about Oct 11–19 in 2026, unverified) is not a holiday, but staff fast and late-night garba lowers lunch orders. Offer farali (fasting) items: sabudana khichdi, rajgira roti, farali pattice.
notes.fasting: Jain Paryushan (about 8 days ending at Samvatsari) and Shravan month bring demand for Jain and no-onion/garlic meals.
notes.weather: Summer (April–June) often exceeds 42°C in Ahmedabad. Keep hot holding to 90 minutes or less and send chaas and cold items in insulated bags. Monsoon (July–September) brings waterlogging, so add a delivery buffer.
notes.plasticBan: Gujarat enforces the national single-use plastic ban (July 2022). Use bagasse, paper or reusable steel packaging.
notes.fssaiLicence: A central kitchen serving corporate clients needs an FSSAI State licence (or Central, depending on turnover/capacity). Show the 14-digit licence number on box labels and invoices.
notes.holidayCaveat: Gujarat had not published its official 2027 holiday list as of 2026-10-03. Entries marked 'tentative' or 'verified-central' come from the Central DoPT 2027 list, panchang calendars or estimates and must be re-checked once the Gujarat GAD 2027 notification is out (usually Nov–Dec of the previous year).
